title: Lester comes to Washington with Basie in 1937 looking for Phil and Pete
summary: In March 1937 Lester, at the Howard Theatre with Basie, asks Booker Coleman for Phillips and Otto Jones and is driven out to the Hanger Club, which had just closed for the night.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Before we get into that, why don't we get into the D.C. scene. You and Pete Jones had been around, and Red Elkins, and you guys had heard Lester Young out West, and a lot of the D.C. people like Paul Jones, the tenor player, had not heard Lester Young yet.
So you'd been telling them about him all this time.
You were telling me a little while ago about that story when Lester Young came up to 7th and T, the first time he ever did a jam session around here -- he came to town with Basie.
When was that? Could you go ahead and tell us that story?

That was in 1937. Must have been something like in March or something like that. Basie was booked at the Howard Theatre, and they had a day layover before they went in the theatre a couple of days. He was looking for me, and so

he asked... He went up to a place where there was jamming, and Booker Coleman was up there playing piano. So he asked Booker, "Do you know some musicians around here named Otto Jones and Leonard Phillips?" Booker said, "Yeah! You're talkin' about Pete and Phil." He said, "Yeah. Sure I know 'em. They're my good friends." Les said, "Can you tell me where I can get in contact with them?" Booker said, "Yeah, I can tell you. Come on, get in a car. I'm going to take you out where Phil's playing." So he brought him out... I was playing at the Hanger Club then. So he brought him...
Across the Fourteenth Street Bridge, in Virginia.

Yeah, that old bridge. So they started out there, but they didn't get out there.... Oh yeah. They went out there, and we had closed. That's what it was. We closed at 2, and when they got out there we just had left. But Booker came on up to my house. He knew where I lived. And just as he got up there, we was getting out -- me and Julius Pogue, a tenor player. We was working on the job together. At this time we wasn't with Booker. We was with Briscoe...
No, not Teddy. Dennis Briscoe. We called him Tex. Everybody called him Tex Briscoe.
You're talking about the bass player?

Yeah, at the Hanger Club. He had the band out there; Booker didn't have it then. So Booker brought Prez up there looking for us. I said "Lester." Ain't no Prez anyway. He went up there looking for us. So he's the one that found us. When they found us, that's when Booker... He went in the house, and we... He knew my wife.
